# Learning materials

> How to write material meant to be learned (a lesson, worked examples, an exercise sheet, a study guide, flashcards, and the questions inside them) so that someone who studies it alone retains it and uses it on new problems. It extends the reader-ergonomics standard; four multivocal reviews (420 sources) give the evidence for five shapes of study documents and their checks.

Each page's markdown source is served at the same path with a .md extension. This index is written by hand; AGENTS.md says to keep it in step.

## The repository

- [Learning materials](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/README.md): scope, where it sits, the four reviews, what it takes from its siblings
- [Decisions](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/decisions/README.md): one record per choice that shapes the repository

## Shapes

- [Shapes](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/README.md): the five shapes, how they fit together, the markup the checks read
- [Lesson](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/lesson.md): objectives, the explanation with its traps refuted, a question block per part, key points
- [Question block](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/question-block.md): recall and application questions, tagged by objective, answers folded and explained
- [Exercise sheet](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/exercise-sheet.md): worked example, completion problem, problems per type; a mixed review; hints before answers
- [Deck](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/deck.md): a header page and a TSV of cards, one question and one answer each, linked to their sections
- [Study guide](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/study-guide.md): one problem solved per type, traps, variants, an error grid, a date to redo, a method sheet
- [Examples](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/shapes/examples/README.md): one document of each shape, on binary search

## Evidence

- [Evidence](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/README.md): the four reviews and the method they share
- [Practice questions](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/practice-questions/README.md): how the questions inside study material are written, placed and answered
- [Flashcards](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/flashcards/README.md): how prompts for spaced review are written, made and kept
- [Exercise sets](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/exercise-sets/README.md): how a set of exercises is ordered and supported, from worked example to problem
- [Instructional text](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/instructional-text/README.md): how an explanatory text is built around its content: objectives, terms, summaries, boxes
- [Bibliography](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics-learning/evidence/bibliography.md): every cited work, once
